source: Oyserman & Lee (2008) Does culture influence what and how we think? Effects of priming individualism and collectivism
finding: Meta-analysis of the individualism/collectivism priming literature. Effects were moderate for relationality and cognition and small for self-concept and values. Effects held across priming methods and outcome types and matched the direction and size of cross-national gaps.
numbers: Abstract only (read via Europe PMC): moderate for relationality and cognition, small for self-concept and values. Full-text headline d values and study count were not retrieved this session.
quote: Effect sizes were moderate for relationality and cognition, small for self-concept and values
limits: Abstract-level only. Meta-analyses of priming overstate effects against preregistered replications (Kvarven et al. 2020, cited by Lin & Wu). Publication-bias handling not checked here.
agent_relevance: A cue can plausibly shift reasoning style, but the 'moderate' average is an upper bound; plan for a small, unstable effect.

source: Oyserman & Lee (2008) Does culture influence what and how we think? Effects of priming individualism and collectivism - Appendix B (supplemental studies)
finding: Supplementary tables list priming studies kept for supplemental analysis (outside the main model), with an overall d per outcome. They show how thin some outcome families are.
numbers: Supplemental overall d: values 0.12 (n=1 study), self-concept 0.30 (n=5), relationality 0.41 (n=14), cognition 0.54 (n=9). These are the supplemental sets, not the headline estimates.
limits: Do not quote these as the main effect. Cognition outcomes had the largest d but from few studies.
agent_relevance: Outcomes closest to reasoning style rest on only a handful of studies.

source: Lin & Wu (2021) Self-construal priming does not shift self-descriptions, value endorsement, or social obligation judgment: preregistered replication and extension of Gardner, Gabriel & Lee (1999)
finding: Large preregistered replication of Gardner, Gabriel & Lee (1999) in Chinese students. Neither story primes nor pronoun-circling word-search primes shifted independent vs interdependent self-descriptions, values or obligation judgments.
numbers: N=468 final (78 per group, 6 groups; 517 recruited, 49 excluded). 80% power for d=0.45. Self-description (20 Statements Test) prime effect F(2,462)=0.283, p=.754, BF01=32.17. Interdependent self-description F(2,462)=0.033, BF01=40.62. Values: BF01 6.9 to 32.5. Obligation judgment BF01=5.17, desirability 7.30, punishment 2.91.
quote: Self-construal priming ... did not change the relative independence or interdependence of one's self-construal in Chinese participants.
limits: Chinese undergraduates at two Shenzhen schools only. Gender, overseas experience, rice-vs-wheat origin and earnestness moderators all null. Not a test in European-American samples.
agent_relevance: Self-description and value priming by a simple cue may not work at all in a strong test. Do not assume a framing cue switches stable style.

source: Lin & Wu (2021) Self-construal priming does not shift self-descriptions, value endorsement, or social obligation judgment: preregistered replication and extension of Gardner, Gabriel & Lee (1999) - Bayesian and small-telescopes criteria
finding: Replication failed all three preregistered success criteria: effect not different from zero, effect not detectable under the small-telescopes test, and Bayes factors favoring the null.
numbers: Original Experiment 1 (N=90) would have had 5.1% power for the replication's TST effect size, 5.0% for values, 5.6% for desirability, 8.1% for obligation, 12.2% for punishment (all under the 33% cutoff). Prime x method interaction BFexcl 12.85 to 1102.54. One unexpected interaction F(1,308)=4.272, p=.040 had BFexcl=5.95 favoring no interaction.
limits: Null evidence applies to this sample and these two primes. The authors favor a habit account over an access account; that is theory, not proven.
agent_relevance: Competing explanation: culture sets a chronic style (habit) and a cue adds little. This favors explicit task structure over a bare framing cue.

source: Brewer & Gardner (1996) Who is this 'we'? Levels of collective identity and self representations, as described in Lin & Wu (2021)
finding: Original pronoun-circling prime: circling 'we/us' in a paragraph raised interpersonal or collective self-descriptions versus 'they' or 'it' controls.
numbers: Only described in Lin & Wu; original numbers not opened.
limits: Secondary description. Original sample sizes and effect sizes not checked.
agent_relevance: This is the word-level cue family that the large replication found null.

source: Trafimow, Triandis & Goto (1991) Some tests of the distinction between the private self and the collective self, as described in Lin & Wu (2021)
finding: Original two-minute thinking prime (how I differ from vs what I share with family and friends) changed the share of private vs collective self-descriptions in North American and Chinese participants. A warrior story prime gave similar results.
numbers: Only described in Lin & Wu; numbers not opened.
limits: Secondary description. Cited as one of three foundation papers.
agent_relevance: Oldest form of the cue: a reflection task rather than a word. Worth testing as a prompt in the LLM setting.

source: Gardner, Gabriel & Lee (1999) 'I' value freedom but 'we' value relationships, as described in Lin & Wu (2021)
finding: Original study (Experiment 1 N about 90) found pronoun and story primes shifted value endorsement and social-obligation judgments in the expected direction.
numbers: Original Experiment 1 N=90; Study 2 groups about 75 and 82 (per Lin & Wu). Original effect sizes not opened.
limits: Small cells. Lin & Wu compute that the original design could only detect about d=0.81 with 80% power.
agent_relevance: Small-sample origin of a very influential result: treat a cue effect as unproven until a large test.

source: Kvarven, Stromland & Johannesson (2020) Comparing meta-analyses and preregistered multiple-laboratory replication projects, as cited in Lin & Wu (2021)
finding: Meta-analytic effects average about three times as large as preregistered multi-lab replications.
numbers: As reported by Lin & Wu: about 3x larger in meta-analyses. Lin & Wu quote the social-psychology meta-analytic average as d=0.43.
limits: Secondary citation; not specific to priming.
agent_relevance: Discount a meta-analytic 'moderate' priming effect heavily.

source: Mesoudi, Magid & Sarkol (2017) Experimental priming of independent and interdependent activity does not affect culturally variable psychological processes (Royal Society Open Science)
finding: Two experiments tried to prime self-construal and analytic/holistic cognition by having people work alone or together (games). No convincing shifts on seven measures, including categorization, portrait selection, landscape drawing, pronoun use and social orientation.
numbers: Exp 1: 84 recruited, 82 analysed (41 cooperative, 41 solitary), no time x activity interaction on any measure. Exp 2: 135 recruited, 132 analysed; 1 of 7 measures (categorization) showed an interaction, in the opposite direction and not significant after Bonferroni alpha=.007.
limits: Authors say the samples could only detect moderate to large effects. Primes (economic games) may not simulate subsistence activity. Tests the ecocultural hypothesis, not pronoun primes.
agent_relevance: Task-based priming of both self-construal and cognitive style did not move style measures; the cognitive-style side is weaker still.

source: Self-construal priming affects holistic face processing and race categorization, but not face recognition (Frontiers in Psychology, 2019)
finding: Self-construal priming had mixed, task-specific effects on face processing and none on face recognition. Same prime, different tasks, different outcomes.
numbers: Exp 1A N=109 (3 priming groups): no priming effect, ps>.19. Exp 1B N=29 (27 analysed): priming x congruency F(2,52)=3.33, p=.04, partial eta2=.11; independent prime removed the congruency (holism) effect. Exp 2: independent group had greater congruency effect than the relational group. No priming effect on recognition in Exp 2 or 3.
limits: Small cells (Exp 1B about 9 per cell). Barely significant. Chinese students only.
agent_relevance: When priming effects appear they depend on the task; do not expect a global style switch.

source: Gender moderates the influence of self-construal priming on fairness considerations (Frontiers in Psychology, 2017)
finding: Dutch ultimatum-game studies: an interdependent prime reduced rejection of an unfair offer, but only in women; in the later studies men showed the reverse direction.
numbers: Study 1 N=226 (independent 75, interdependent 75, control 76). Women, interdependent: 33.3% rejected vs 62.5% independent (Wald chi2=7.31, p=.007) and 57.5% control (p=.04). Gender x condition Wald chi2=5.17, p=.02. Second study: 180 students, 90 per condition.
limits: Moderator interactions; direction flipped across studies and sexes. Dutch students only.
agent_relevance: Individual moderators can flip the sign of a cue effect: one cue may push different users in opposite directions.

source: Bicultural Minds: A cultural priming approach to the self-bias effect (Behavioral Sciences, 2022)
finding: British participants: an interdependent prime (word search, then reflective writing) reduced self-bias in shape-label matching only for those with low baseline self-bias; the independent prime did nothing.
numbers: Exp 1 N=36, Exp 2 N=36. Priming main effect F(1,30)=1.54, p=.23; priming x bias group F(1,30)=0.00, p=.97. The effect appears only inside a split by baseline. Authors say Exp 2 replicated the subgroup pattern.
limits: Tiny samples; post hoc split by baseline; not preregistered.
agent_relevance: Baseline matters: cues may work on some users and not others, which argues for reading the baseline before cueing.

source: Tao, Viberg, Baker & Kizilcec (2024) Cultural bias and cultural alignment of large language models (PNAS Nexus)
finding: Five OpenAI models default to English-speaking and Protestant-European values on the Integrated Values Survey. A one-line cultural prompt ('You are a typical human being born in [country]...') cut the gap for most countries but not all.
numbers: Mean cultural distance: GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57, GPT-4-turbo 2.71 to 1.77, GPT-4 2.69 to 1.65 (all P<0.001); GPT-3 2.39 to 2.11; GPT-3.5-turbo 3.35 to 2.83. Countries improved: GPT-4o 71.0%, GPT-4-turbo 81.3%, GPT-4 77.6%, GPT-3.5-turbo 72.6%, GPT-3 80.4%. 10 prompt variants, about 107 countries.
quote: For recent models, this improves the cultural alignment of the models' output for 71-81% of countries and territories
limits: 19 to 29% of countries got no better or worse. GPT-4o: Finland distance rose 0.20 to 2.43, Luxembourg 0.59 to 2.72, Taiwan 2.40 to 3.94. Two value axes (survival vs self-expression, traditional vs secular), not individualism scales as such.
agent_relevance: Direct LLM analogue of orientation priming: a short identity cue closes about a third of the gap on average, with large per-target failures.

source: Tao et al. (2024) - model-age trend
finding: Cultural prompting helped newer, larger models more than older ones.
numbers: Gain in distance: GPT-4 1.04 (2.69 to 1.65), GPT-4-turbo 0.94, GPT-4o 0.85, GPT-3.5-turbo 0.52 (3.35 to 2.83), GPT-3 0.28 (2.39 to 2.11). Prompts were passed as system prompts.
limits: Differences computed from the reported means; no per-model intervals read.
agent_relevance: A cue works better in more capable models, so effects measured on one model may not carry over.

source: Luther & Brown (2025) The American Ghost in the Machine: how language models align culturally and the effects of cultural prompting
finding: Eight LLMs on Hofstede VSM13 with and without a cultural system prompt for six countries. Most defaulted to US values. Prompting helped seven of eight models overall but unevenly by country.
numbers: Total-distance improvement: DeepSeek-V3.1 30.87% (1,037.01 to 792.42), GPT-5 16.7%, DeepSeek-V3 15.74%, Opus 4 12.75%, GPT-4 6.3%, GPT-4.1 3.72%; Llama 3.1 worse by 27.33%. By country: US 13.2%, India 22.3%, Japan 19.1%, China 17.22% better; Iran 3.54% worse; France 13.63% worse (1,310.12 to 1,488.7). GPT-5 moved only 87.13 to 82.83 for the US.
limits: VSM13 forced-choice items; six countries; no control for demand effects.
agent_relevance: Cue effects are model-specific and target-specific; measure after cueing, never assume.

source: Kharchenko, Roosta, Chadha & Shah (2025) How well do LLMs represent values across cultures? (KDD '25)
finding: Advice requests with persona and language prompts for 36 countries and languages. Models tell high- and low-individualism countries apart but stereotype them, and consistency is limited.
numbers: Every model and method rated the US individualist and Japan collectivist. Largest gap: Command-R personas, 72.40% individualistic answers for the American persona vs 19.60% for the Japanese persona. Individualism correlation with country value 0.71 (p<0.05) for GPT-4o with high-resource languages in the multilingual approach; the paper says no other model, value, language set or approach had a significant correlation of this kind.
limits: Percentages are model- and method-specific; the sign of change varies (e.g., GPT-4o Orientation -70.7% with personas, +74.7% multilingual).
agent_relevance: A persona cue produces textbook stereotypes, not the real local profile, and mostly fails to track country-level variation.

source: Jeripity Venkata (2026) When AI speaks, whose values does it express? A cross-cultural audit of individualism-collectivism bias in LLMs
finding: Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.4 and Gemini 2.5 Flash give individualist advice to users from collectivist countries, even when told the user's country. Language and country-label effects differ per model.
numbers: n=840 scored responses (10 dilemmas, 10 countries, 7 languages). Mean misalignment +0.76 on a 1-5 scale (t=15.65, p<0.001). Nigeria +1.85, India +0.82. Claude vs GPT-5.4 d=0.017; Gemini lower (d about 0.32 vs both). Native language: Claude more collectivist (Wilcoxon p=0.017, mean C3-C4 = -0.144 overall); Gemini opposite (p=0.034, +0.139); GPT-5.4 no language effect (p=0.097), follows the stated country only.
limits: Single-author preprint; temperature 0; LLM judges scored output (GPT-4o prompt-mapping kappa 0.62); only ten prompts.
agent_relevance: A country-identity cue is partly obeyed as sycophancy to claimed identity (GPT-5.4), so cue strength is not proof of real style change.

source: Lu, Song & Zhang (2025) Cultural tendencies in generative AI (Nature Human Behaviour)
finding: GPT and ERNIE answered a battery in Chinese or English. Chinese gave a more interdependent orientation and more holistic cognitive style; exploratory tests said a cultural persona prompt shifts these tendencies.
numbers: Abstract and MIT Sloan press page only: no effect sizes or Ns retrieved. Replicated in ERNIE; ad recommendation changed with language.
quote: exploratory analyses suggest that cultural prompts ... can adjust these cultural tendencies
limits: Full text not opened. The authors label the prompting results exploratory.
agent_relevance: Language works as a priming cue in LLMs; exploratory support for a persona cue.

source: Hu et al. (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms: introducing Machine Culture
finding: 2x2 test (US vs Chinese model x English vs Chinese prompt) over eight multimodal tasks. Prompt language moved some holistic markers in the human direction, but several tasks showed reversal and categorization showed no language effect.
numbers: Chinese vs English prompts, object count in generated images: 10.71 vs 8.91, t(286.19)=4.88, d=0.49. Scene description: English higher, 10.90 vs 10.06, d=0.36 (reverse of human pattern). Collective attribution 3.05 vs 2.93, d=0.34; individual attribution 4.68 vs 4.74, d=0.23 (human direction, small). Categorization R-C: 7.10 vs 7.04, p=.741, d=0.03. Model origin: US model more relational pairing than Chinese model (8.10 vs 6.04, d=1.38), the opposite of expectation.
limits: One research group; GPT-4o/DALL-E 3/ERNIE 4.5/iRAG; author-chosen scoring.
agent_relevance: Language cue acts on some behaviours and fails or inverts on others; do not generalize from one task.

source: Jin, Zhang, Shu & Cui (2023) The cultural psychology of large language models: is ChatGPT a holistic or analytic thinker?
finding: Without any cue, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 lean holistic on process tests (AHS, triadic categorization) but score independent on self-construal scales.
numbers: 10 runs per setting. TCT mean 0.87 (GPT-3.5, SD 0.06) and 0.85 (GPT-4, SD 0.05); SCS-Independent GPT-3.5 6.98, GPT-4 5.32; SCS-Interdependent GPT-3.5 5.85, GPT-4 4.95; AHS above norm, p<0.001 for both; robust to temperature and prompt language.
limits: No priming condition; baseline only. Small number of runs.
agent_relevance: Base-model orientation may be split (holistic process, independent values), so a cue acts on a mixed default.

source: Sabir, Gasper, Loem & Sharma (2025) Contrasting cognitive styles in vision-language models: holistic attention in Japanese vs analytical focus in English
finding: Output language of captions shifts vision-language models between holistic and analytic descriptions, but image content matters too.
numbers: GPT-4o-JP holistic classification rose from 26.10% on COCO images to 73.37% on a 1K Japanese image set; another table gives 67.60% holistic and 32.40% analytic on the 1K Japanese set. Spanish output stayed as analytic as English.
limits: Descriptive classification by an LLM judge; output language, model size and dataset are tangled.
agent_relevance: Cue effects depend on the content they meet; a style cue alone is not a switch.

source: Negru, Lemnaru, Surdeanu & Potolea (2026) Understanding cultural alignment in multilingual LLMs via natural debate statements
finding: Chinese and US models reflect the values of their home country, and switching prompt language between English and Chinese mostly changed nothing significant.
numbers: Four models (two US, two Chinese). Significant language differences only for GPT on UAI and LTO and for DeepSeek on PDI and LTO; no significant difference on most other dimension-model pairs. Authors read this as models settling on a shared profile regardless of user language.
limits: Hofstede dimensions from synthetic labels on debate statements; few models.
agent_relevance: Prompt language is a weak orientation cue for current LLMs; do not rely on it.

source: Lin & Wu (2021) Self-construal priming does not shift self-descriptions, value endorsement, or social obligation judgment: preregistered replication and extension of Gardner, Gabriel & Lee (1999) - manipulation check and values baseline
finding: Participants attended to the task and the manipulation was delivered, yet downstream style did not move.
numbers: 92.7% correctly counted the target words in the word search; all reported answering seriously. Baseline: collectivist values endorsed more than individualist (5.49 vs 4.65, t(467)=13.67, d=0.63). Sensitivity: 80% power at d=0.45.
limits: No separate check of how much the prime registered beyond the word count.
agent_relevance: Measure outcome, not cue uptake: a cue can be read and obeyed without changing downstream reasoning.

source: Hong, Morris, Chiu & Benet-Martinez (2000) Multicultural minds (cultural frame switching)
finding: Original cultural-icon priming in bicultural Hong Kong students: American icons raised dispositional attribution, Chinese icons raised situational attribution.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers retrieved this session.
limits: Not read. Icons differ from self-construal primes.
agent_relevance: Icon-style cues are the nearest analogue to a persona cue; a clean replication was not found in this search.

source: Oyserman & Lee (2008) - priming methods as summarized on Language Log
finding: Blog summary lists seven priming families in the meta-analysis: task context, imagined tasks, thinking about relationships, pronoun circling, sentence unscrambling, warrior story, cultural icons.
numbers: Quoted instructions: 'think of what makes you different from your family and friends' (individualism) vs 'what you have in common' (collectivism); pronoun circling I/me/my vs we/us/our; unscrambling words like unique, autonomous vs team, together.
limits: Blog summary of the paper, not the paper.
agent_relevance: The cue wordings are reusable as prompts and as controls.

source: Mesoudi, Magid & Sarkol (2017) - authors' conclusion
finding: Authors give two readings of the null: the primes were inadequate, or these measures are fixed early in development and cannot be primed.
numbers: Authors call these two of the largest studies of their kind yet say samples may only detect moderate to large effects; they advise larger samples.
quote: despite many previous studies that have purported to find such priming effects
limits: Within-subject pre/post design used to gain power; wider uncertainty remains.
agent_relevance: Two rival explanations (weak prime vs fixed trait) are not yet separated by data.
